openings.claim: Unreliable reservation-to-location addresses may explain repeat searches; fresh cart addresses could explain O4. Repair the current locator on book moves while retaining surname dividers.
openings.discriminator: Match size, candidate count and load: wrong addresses should prolong searching; reliable shelf/cart addresses should converge. Persistent slow reliable addresses weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Clerk records arrival, service start, search, completion, address accuracy, second searches, size/count and update work on existing paper; compare matched ordinary pickups before/during locator updates. Verify recipients, keep identities behind desk, retain two shelves/cart, cap all preparation/corrections at ten minutes; stop if exceeded.
openings.uncertainty: Reservation identity checking capability, feasible recording, matched episodes and sustained update workload are unconfirmed.

openings.claim: Candidate density and handling difficulty may dominate; small accessible arrival batches could explain cart speed, with address errors secondary.
openings.discriminator: At matched address accuracy and size, density should predict search duration; comparable density should erase cart advantage. Strong wrong-address delays without a density gradient defeat this account.
openings.probe: Use D1 observational records and matching comparisons.
openings.uncertainty: Cart volume, book-size explanation and sufficient matched episodes remain unverified.

openings.claim: The concentrated arrival burst may dominate total pickup delays despite accurate locations.
openings.discriminator: Locator improvements shorten searching, but peak-window waits persist while the sole clerk is occupied; little search time in slow verified pickups weakens the address explanation.
openings.probe: Use D1 arrival/service/completion records to separate waiting from retrieval across comparable load.

Retains address mechanism and density-matched discriminator.

decision: Compare address accuracy, density and waiting before choosing a remedy. All evidence is synthetic; bounded probe fit proves neither reduced clerk burden nor the target of 95% within two minutes with no wrong-reader handoffs. Reader presence uncertainty and sample representativeness remain unresolved.
